content.value_statement: Metabase documentation needs clear, consistent wording for many reader levels. This skill guides drafts, edits, examples, links, and formatting in Metabase documentation style.
actual_capabilities: Guides drafts for Metabase Markdown and MDX documentation.
Applies reader-focused voice, heading, link, and UI text rules.
Prompts writers to define audience needs before drafting.
Provides reusable examples for instructions, headings, links, and wording.
Recommends Prettier formatting after documentation edits.
limitations: Does not validate Metabase behavior without project context.
Depends on a shared Metabase style guide reference.
May request a local formatter command that needs user approval.
Does not replace product, engineering, or legal review.

use_cases.title: Draft Feature Documentation
use_cases.description: Create a first draft for a new Metabase feature with direct steps and clear headings.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Docs
use_cases.description: Rewrite formal or vague documentation so it matches Metabase voice and reader needs.

use_cases.title: Review Release Updates
use_cases.description: Check changed docs for examples, links, formatting, and wording before publication.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite a Paragraph
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this Metabase docs paragraph in a clearer, more direct style. Keep the meaning and note any missing context: [paste text]

prompt_templates.title: Draft a New Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Metabase docs draft for [feature]. Audience: [reader]. Goal: [task]. Include headings, steps, examples to verify, and link suggestions.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing MDX File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [file path or pasted content] against the Metabase documentation style. Return prioritized edits for clarity, headings, links, examples, and formatting.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Complex Documentation Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan documentation updates for [release or feature set]. Identify affected pages, reader tasks, example checks, wording risks, and a publishing checklist.

output_examples.input: A paragraph uses formal wording and vague headings.
output_examples.output: The response gives a clearer paragraph, a stronger action-oriented heading, and notes where more product detail is needed.

output_examples.input: A new feature needs a documentation outline.
A reviewer asks whether a docs page is ready.
output_examples.output: The response lists blocking issues, small wording fixes, formatting tasks, and final review questions.

best_practices: Identify the reader and task before writing.
Verify commands, examples, images, and links before publication.
Ask before running any local formatter or command.
anti_patterns: Do not bury required steps inside long paragraphs.
Do not call tasks easy or obvious.
Do not publish untested examples or outdated numbers.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps write and edit Metabase documentation in a clear, reader-focused style.

faq.question: Can it edit Markdown and MDX files?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed for documentation files such as Markdown and MDX.

faq.question: Does it verify product behavior?
faq.answer: No. You should confirm feature behavior, examples, and screenshots with the product or code.

faq.question: Will it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It may suggest a Prettier command. Review and approve local commands before execution.

faq.question: Is it only for Metabase?
faq.answer: Its guidance is specific to Metabase documentation style, but some writing principles are general.

faq.question: How should reviewers use it?
faq.answer: Ask for a focused review of clarity, headings, links, examples, formatting, and reader fit.
